name: Jehoahaz (Shallum) of Judah
charge: Doing evil in the sight of the Lord according to all that his fathers had done
summary: After Josiah fell at Megiddo the people of the land anointed his son Jehoahaz, called Shallum, and in three months he did evil according to all his fathers had done (2 Kings 23:30-32). Pharaoh Necho put him in bands at Riblah, laid a tribute on the land, set his brother Eliakim on the throne as Jehoiakim, and carried Jehoahaz to Egypt, where he died (2 Kings 23:33-34). Jeremiah told the people to weep not for the dead king but for the one who went away, for he would never see his native land again (Jeremiah 22:10-12).
offenseFull: Josiah was carried dead from Megiddo, and the people of the land took Jehoahaz his son, anointed him and made him king in his father’s place (2 Kings 23:30). The people did this themselves, and they passed over the elder brother: Jehoahaz was twenty-three and Jehoiakim twenty-five (2 Kings 23:31, 36). The curse had said the Lord would bring them and the king they set over themselves into a nation they had not known (Deuteronomy 28:36), and this king is an example of it. He reigned three months and did evil according to all that his fathers had done (2 Kings 23:31-32). He followed the wicked kings, not his father who had turned to the Lord with all his heart.

Ezekiel took up a lamentation for the princes of Israel: their mother was a lioness who raised a whelp among the young lions, and he learned to catch the prey and devoured men; the nations heard of him, he was taken in their pit, and they brought him with chains to the land of Egypt (Ezekiel 19:1-4). That is Jehoahaz. Like Nimrod, the mighty hunter, he led men, the nation, into evil. Jeremiah was sent to the king’s house in those days with the terms on which the house of David would stand: execute judgment and righteousness, deliver the oppressed, do no violence to the stranger, the fatherless or the widow, and shed no innocent blood; if they would not hear, the house would become a desolation (Jeremiah 22:1-5).
judgmentFull: Pharaoh Necho put him in bands at Riblah in the land of Hamath, in Syria, so that he could not reign in Jerusalem, and laid on the land a tribute of a hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold. He made Eliakim, Josiah’s other son, king and changed his name to Jehoiakim, and took Jehoahaz to Egypt, where he died (2 Kings 23:33-34; 2 Chronicles 36:3-4). Jehoiakim paid Pharaoh by taxing the people, exacting silver and gold from every man according to his assessment (2 Kings 23:35), and he too did evil like his forefathers.

The word concerning Shallum the son of Josiah, who reigned in place of his father, was that the people should not weep for the dead, but weep bitterly for the one who went away: he had gone out of that place and would not return, but would die where they led him captive and see the land no more (Jeremiah 22:10-12). Shallum means retribution. Josiah was buried among his fathers; his son was buried in Egypt, the house of bondage the Lord had brought Israel out of. A father’s crown could not keep a son who would not keep his father’s course.

text.text: And his servants carried him in a chariot dead from Megiddo, and brought him to Jerusalem, and buried him in his own sepulchre. And the people of the land took Jehoahaz the son of Josiah, and anointed him, and made him king in his father’s stead.
Jehoahaz was twenty and three years old when he began to reign; and he reigned three months in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, according to all that his fathers had done.
And Pharaoh–nechoh put him in bands at Riblah in the land of Hamath, that he might not reign in Jerusalem; and put the land to a tribute of an hundred talents of silver, and a talent of gold.
And Pharaoh–nechoh made Eliakim the son of Josiah king in the room of Josiah his father, and turned his name to Jehoiakim, and took Jehoahaz away: and he came to Egypt, and died there.
Weep ye not for the dead, neither bemoan him: but weep sore for him that goeth away: for he shall return no more, nor see his native country.
For thus saith the Lord touching Shallum the son of Josiah king of Judah, which reigned instead of Josiah his father, which went forth out of this place; He shall not return thither any more:
But he shall die in the place whither they have led him captive, and shall see this land no more.

Jehoiakim was twenty and five years old when he began to reign; and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Zebudah, the daughter of Pedaiah of Rumah.
The Lord shall bring thee, and thy king which thou shalt set over thee, unto a nation which neither thou nor thy fathers have known; and there shalt thou serve other gods, wood and stone.

Moreover take thou up a lamentation for the princes of Israel,
And say, What is thy mother? A lioness: she lay down among lions, she nourished her whelps among young lions.
And she brought up one of her whelps: it became a young lion, and it learned to catch the prey; it devoured men.
The nations also heard of him; he was taken in their pit, and they brought him with chains unto the land of Egypt.
Thus saith the Lord; Go down to the house of the king of Judah, and speak there this word,
And say, Hear the word of the Lord, O king of Judah, that sittest upon the throne of David, thou, and thy servants, and thy people that enter in by these gates:

Thus saith the Lord; Execute ye judgment and righteousness, and deliver the spoiled out of the hand of the oppressor: and do no wrong, do no violence to the stranger, the fatherless, nor the widow, neither shed innocent blood in this place.
For if ye do this thing indeed, then shall there enter in by the gates of this house kings sitting upon the throne of David, riding in chariots and on horses, he, and his servants, and his people.
But if ye will not hear these words, I swear by myself, saith the Lord, that this house shall become a desolation.
